title: Quarterly Focus & Velocity Journal — Evelyn Park
content:
Purpose: a lightweight, private scratchpad to track growth levers I own this quarter — focus, small experiments, and weekly velocity rituals. Not polished; meant for quick capture, triage, and handoff notes.

Quarter goals (working drafts) — quarter target: Q3 2025
1) Reduce p99 inference latency for hosted text-gen (target: -12% from baseline)
   - Baseline: p99 = ~240ms for 1K-token requests (sampled). Target p99 <= 212ms.
   - Success signals: p99 down month-over-month, no user-facing quality regressions, cost delta < +5%.

2) Ship and measure latency-aware batching heuristic (experiment)
   - Hypothesis: dynamic thresholding + micro-batching reduces tail latency for bursty traffic without harming throughput.
   - Metric: % requests hitting latency SLO and cost per token on A/B. Target: reduce cost-per-token for low-latency tier by 6–10%.

3) Improve personal engineering throughput and handoffs
   - Goal: consistent 3 code review completions/week and 1 small ship every 2 weeks.
   - Success signals: fewer review back-and-forths; more PRs merged without rework; improved teammate satisfaction score (qualitative).

Habit & velocity tracker (daily micro-items) — X = done
- Morning: 30m focused on experiments (X)
- Noon: triage PR queue (15m)
- End of day: update this doc + 5 minute retro

Experiment log (scratchpad)
- Experiment: dynamic-batch-threshold v0.3
  - Started: 2025-07-10
  - Variant A: static threshold 8ms, Variant B: adaptive algorithm (p95-based multiplier)
  - Early observation (2025-07-17): Variant B reduced avg queue time by ~9% but increased jitter on small requests. Need to tighten fallback for <256 token requests.
  - Next step: add a localized fallback to keep requests <256 tokens on low-latency path.

- Experiment: kv-cache-size-tuning
  - Started: 2025-08-02
  - Note: observed ~3% cost improvement when keeping hot prefixes in LRU for 48h. Watch for miss-rate increase after purge window.

Decision log (for handoffs)
- 2025-08-20: decided to push batch-threshold rollout to canary stage after proxy-level metric checks. Reason: jitter on internal tool traffic caused spikes in p50 for small requests. Owner: Evelyn. Action: create ENG-PR-4128 to add circuit-breaker.

Retro (monthly) — 2025-09-30
- Wins:
  * Got kv-cache tuning into prod canary with no user regressions.
  * Reduced noisy alerts from experiment infra by adding rate-limits on metrics emission.
- Failures / learnings:
  * Underestimated amount of noise in small-request traffic; should have included a developer traffic cohort earlier.
  * My weekly habit drifted in late August — need stricter blocking windows.
- Changes for next quarter:
  * Formalize a 2-hour weekly experimentation block in calendar (no meetings).
  * Pair with Maya for rollout checklist so handoffs are smoother.

Action items (running)
- [ ] ENG-PR-4128: add circuit-breaker for adaptive batch path (owner: Evelyn) — due 2025-10-09
- [x] Write initial experiment notes and share with Ravi — done 2025-07-12
- [ ] Create dashboard for per-model small-request jitter (owner: Ravi) — blocked (needs metrics team)

Misc short notes (brain dump)
- Slack follow-ups: ask @mike about infra quota for canary GPUs.
- Link to related: CONFLUENCE-optimizations/latency-playbook (bookmark for rollout checklist).
- Remind: be explicit about acceptable cost delta when proposing latency optimizations (+/- 5% threshold).

Personal reflection (one-paragraph)
Quick note to self: velocity doesn't mean busy-ness. Focus on a few measurable bets and the smallest possible experiments that teach. When distracted, return to this doc and force a 5-minute review of the top 3 outcomes.
